review_method: Used the existing complete 696-unit pinned inventory before reviewing all 137 actual source units. Read every full source, proposed target and necessary context, including all of the actual Greek-numbered Psalm 17; 1 Chronicles 20:4-8, all of 21 and 11:10-47; Joshua 9:15-21; Numbers 35:33; Deuteronomy 24:16; 1 Samuel 16:10-13, 17:4-7, 20:14-17, 26:6 and 31:12-13; Acts 1:15-20; Romans 15:8-12; 2 Samuel 2:18, 7:12-16, 11:3, 15:12 and 18:15; 1 Kings 1:32-38 and 2:35; and 2 Chronicles 3:1. Psalm target locators were selected from actual texts: both 22:2 and 22:3 correspond to Psalm 17:3, and the subsequent selected locators were individually checked rather than imported from presumed Hebrew Psalm 18 numbering. Separately displayed and reread all 140 complete source/target/category/rationale triples in ten untruncated slices. Preserved the complete original draft and seventeen exact refinements, then separately displayed and reread all seventeen full final changed triples. The one changed target at 21:8 was read in full as the actual individual-responsibility rule before retention. Partial textual correspondences preserve differing names, parentage, victims, ranks, counts, crops, physical descriptions, agents, actions, tenses and prices; they do not certify unverified identities or harmonizations. The named local roster and itinerary links concern the express group headings, repeated origin designation or command defining those particular entries, not generic list succession. No exhaustive discovery, original-language, apparatus, independent specialist, medical, modern site, financial conversion or unverified chronological reconstruction is claimed. After independent peer review, preserved the initial frozen TSV and author receipt unchanged, made four exact claim refinements, and separately displayed and reread all four complete corrected source/target/category/rationale triples before this final refreeze. Those changes clarify the lamp prohibition addressed to David, the actual All of them pronoun after the lawless-one context, and Ariel of Moab without an asserted battle location.
